title: Source Specification v1
description: Extraction specification for an InfoSource. Each InfoSource holds a source_specs list; all specs are evaluated against the same fetch group (the InfoSource URL's fetched bytes, not chained off primary extracted output). The first spec is the primary extraction strategy; additional specs are cross-check alternatives for selector-rot detection. All specs in a list must share a content-kind family (html_text: css|xpath; json: jsonpath); full_page is family-neutral and pairs with either. Every algorithm here reaches a co-core extractor that honours it; which media types honour it is the extractor's to say: css on HTML only, xpath on HTML and XML (HTML since co-core 0.38, cannobserv#557), jsonpath on JSON only (cannobserv#354, archiver#356), full_page on anything (one line per item on an RSS or Atom root, one canonical-JSON chunk on a JSON body). jsonpath is RFC 9535 in strict mode: one chunk per matched node, labelled with its normalized path; a string node's text is whitespace-normalized, any other node is canonical JSON. full_page on JSON keeps strings as they are, so the two do not give the same text. regex is refused by co-core. The URL is a separate InfoSource field, not part of this spec.

ignore_selectors.description: CSS selectors removed from the page before the selection, under css, xpath or full_page (never jsonpath, which co-core refuses with them): timestamps, 'last updated' footers, ads, session tokens (cannobserv#570, archiver#378). Only HTML honours them. On an XML feed, PDF or spreadsheet co-core refuses a spec that carries them; this schema can't see the media type, so the preview reports that at /extraction and Processor as extraction_error. Omit the key for none: [] extracts as an absent key does but fingerprints as a different spec, so it is refused here.
